description: §38.1 PRECEDENCE, the visible half of the S353-bryan ruling — `<page>` → nested `<program db=>` → `<channel>` fires NOTHING. The scoped-DB subtree is not extracted, so the channel survives into server emission: the server mounts `/_scrml_ws/page_feed` and the client dials that same route. Before the ruling landed this shape was refused with E-CHANNEL-INSIDE-PAGE even though it works. This is the one row where option (b) has a consequence an author can see, and it is the row a partial implementation leaves behind — moving only the `name=`d case is achievable by ordering a new code ahead of the page check, without ever writing the `pageDepth` reset the ruling names.
rationale: §38.2 normative (S356): "A nested `<program>` SHALL be a fresh `<channel>` placement scope … `<page>` → `<program db=\"…\">` → `<channel>` SHALL emit NEITHER." §4.12.1 is the more specific normative sentence and wins over §38's flat "channels SHALL NOT live inside `<page>`": a nested `<program>` is a separate compilation unit subject to top-level grammar, so a `<channel>` in its body is at canonical placement FOR THAT UNIT. Blast radius was measured at 0 corpus instances across all 2260 `.scrml` (S239), so the ruling was taken on correctness rather than cost.
